irene: hey team :wave: first week here, trying to build the inference runtime from source on my dev VM (ubuntu22, local GPU). getting a ptxas error during make. who should I bug for onboarding tips?

ben: welcome! :tada: can you paste the exact ptxas error and the outputs of `nvcc -V` and `nvidia-smi`?

irene: sure — here's the relevant tail from the build:```/home/irene/work/runtime/build/obj/ops.cu(42): error: ptxas fatal   : Value 'sm_86' is not defined for option 'gpu-name'```build command was `make -j8`.
`nvcc -V` -> "Cuda compilation tools, release 11.4, V11.4.120"
`nvidia-smi` -> "Driver Version: 535.86.10  GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB"

ash: looks like nvcc/toolkit is older than the driver / targeted arch. ptxas from CUDA 11.x doesn't recognize sm_86. quick checks: `which ptxas`, `echo $CUDA_HOME`, and `ls -l /usr/local/cuda`

irene: ran those: `which ptxas` -> `/usr/bin/ptxas` (weird), `echo $CUDA_HOME` -> "" (empty), `/usr/local/cuda` -> symlink to `/usr/local/cuda-11.4`

ben: yep that's the mismatch. two easy paths:
- upgrade the CUDA toolkit to 12.x (recommended for the A100 and sm_86 builds) and point /usr/local/cuda to the new install.
- or change the build arch to only compile for a supported compute capability (e.g., add `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80`), but that loses performance if you have newer hw.
Snippets that helped me: add to `~/.bashrc`: `export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` `export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH` `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` then `hash -r` and `which ptxas` should point to `/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas`

runtime-oncall: if you need system-level installs on that VM I can grant sudo for package install or we can spin up a container with matching CUDA. ping me and @infra-bot will create a ticket for a proper /usr/local/cuda upgrade if infra approval required.

ash: alternatively, for a fast unblock, try our dev docker image: `docker run --gpus all -it --rm --shm-size=1g nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 bash` then `git clone` + `make` inside the container — that isolates host changes.

irene: thanks — I'll try the container first to avoid touching the VM. if that works I'll request the toolkit upgrade so CI/dev machines match. will report back. :+1:

ben: awesome — ping me if the container still hits ptxas issues. also file a tiny runbook PR linking this thread once resolved so future new hires hit fewer snags.

infra-bot: ticket created #INFRA-4321 for CUDA toolkit upgrade on dev pool (requester: irene).
